comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C1-C3, C66-C68, C79, C84, C119 regarding streptavidin signal enhancement. Both evaluations find the evidence solid and well-supported with strong quantitative data demonstrating 2.9-fold signal improvement over anti-HA antibodies.

Strong agreement on claims C4-C7, C30-C31, C49-C61, C110-C111, C146-C147 regarding detection in phase-separated compartments. Both evaluations affirm the experimental verification is solid and demonstrates value for hard-to-label regions across multiple cell types and antibody types.

Agreement on claims C8-C9, C104-C105, C108, C112-C113, C115-C116 regarding systematic nuclear pore mapping. Peer reviewers implicitly accept findings by not raising concerns; OpenEval explicitly supports the comprehensive experimental design with 45 cell lines and dual tagging strategies.

Perfect agreement on claims C74-C79 regarding expansion microscopy applications. Both evaluations find experimental verification solid and highlight particular value for expansion microscopy when signal is limiting.

Agreement on claims C82-C83 regarding CLEM applications. Both evaluations support the findings, with peer reviewers specifically highlighting value for correlative light and electron microscopy when signal is limiting or inaccessible.

Agreement on claims C26-C28, C152-C155 regarding mechanistic explanations for streptavidin advantages. Both evaluations accept these biochemical properties as reasonable explanations grounded in established biophysical principles.

Agreement on claims C42-C43, C48, C123-C127, C130 regarding resolution and labeling specificity. Both evaluations support that the method provides comparable resolution to immunofluorescence with appropriate specificity within the nuclear pore.

Strong agreement on claims C117-C118, C120-C122, C143-C144, C160-C161 regarding broad utility and integration of findings. Both evaluations affirm the method is valuable and useful across multiple applications demonstrated in the study.

Agreement on claims C53-C55 regarding quantitative stress granule findings. Both evaluations accept the quantitative data showing differential detection patterns; peer reviewers describe experimental verification as solid.
Agreement on claims C46-C47 regarding control experiments. Both evaluations support these controls demonstrating low background and specificity, which are essential for validating the method.

Agreement on claims C86-C87, C89, C91, C93, C96-C98 regarding dynamic localization history. Both evaluations support the findings with appropriate caveats; peer reviewers acknowledge valuable revisions toward more cautious phraseology about tracking labeled proteins.

Agreement on claim C87 regarding methodological caveats. Both evaluations support the need for orthogonal validation; peer reviewers specifically acknowledge valuable revisions toward more cautious presentation of limitations.

Divergence on claims C32-C33, C157-C158 regarding specificity of labeling. OpenEval finds evidence supported; peer reviewers raise critical concern that TurboID marks proximal proteins, making it 'formally no longer possible to be certain what the biotin is attached to' and emphasize limitations need to be clear.

Both uncertain on claims C133-C134 regarding resolution trade-offs. OpenEval cites unpublished data as limiting evaluation; peer reviewers' concern about uncertainty of labeled proteins relates to these theoretical considerations about limitations.

OpenEval evaluates claims C100-C103 as uncertain regarding functional interpretation of NUP transport roles, noting observations are clear but functional interpretation is speculative. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific functional claims.

OpenEval evaluates claims C135-C137 as uncertain regarding novelty and priority claims about the literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these novelty assertions.

Partial overlap on claim C122 regarding methodological caveats. OpenEval specifically evaluates this caveat as supported; peer reviewers address it within broader utility discussion (R11), affirming the method is valuable while acknowledging limitations.
